title: Removing a future bleaching-report rule added 21 records but did not establish a future-heat link in four coral samples
abstract: We tested a selection rule in an earlier coral heat study. The earlier test required a future bleaching percentage to obtain future heat. We removed that requirement in BCO-DMO 773466 version 2 and kept the other rules. The four Atlantic and Pacific samples grew from 840 to 861 monthly records in 2003-2018. All corrected future-heat intervals still crossed zero. The early Atlantic slope changed from +5.01 to +15.08 bleaching points per four TSA degree-heating weeks, with a new interval of -15.11 to +45.27. The other three slopes changed little or not at all. Future heat values were unchanged on all common rows. The change came from added rows. Few countries, sparse heat and selection on future visits limit inference. The null tests cannot establish absence of bias. Code rebuilds both samples from hashed external data and reproduces prior estimates.

display.caption: Future-heat estimates and 98.75% country-group intervals before and after removal of the future bleaching-report rule. All four new intervals cross zero. Record counts show the small gain in sample size.
